{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script
#
# This is a self-submitting Flux script: run it directly (e.g., `./train_scratch.flux.sh`).
# It will submit itself to Flux with the translated resource requests.

# Translated resources from LSF:
#   -W 16:00          -> -t 16h
#   -n 8              -> -n 8
#   span[ptile=8]     -> -N 1 (best-effort: keep ranks on one node)
#   -gpu "num=1"      -> -g 1
#   -M 48000 (MB)     -> (not translated; see note)
JOBID=$(flux batch -N 1 -n 8 -g 1 -t 16h --wrap "bash $0 __flux_inner")

echo "Submitted Flux job: $JOBID"

if [ "${1:-}" = "__flux_inner" ]; then
  # NOTE: LSF -q amdgpu not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a queue/constraint mapping, the job may run on any eligible GPU resources; you are not forcing the amdgpu queue.

  # NOTE: LSF -M 48000 (memory) not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a memory reservation/limit, the job may contend for memory or be OOM-killed, affecting reliability/performance.

  # NOTE: LSF -e/-o used %J expansion (jobid) which Flux does not provide portably.
  # Performance implication: none; operational implication: log filenames may not be unique unless you add uniqueness.

  module load bedtools/2.29.2-wrl
  module load gcc/9.3.0
  module load cuda/11.7
  module load samtools/1.6-wrl
  module load pigz/2.6.0
  module load ucsctools
  source activate maxatac

  cd /data/weirauchlab/team/ngun7t/maxatac/runs || exit 1

  # Run within the allocation.
  # NOTE: If training uses multiple ranks, adjust how maxatac is launched.
  flux run -n 8 -g 1 maxatac train --genome hg38 \
    --arch Transformer_phuc \
    --sequence /users/ngun7t/opt/maxatac/data/hg38/hg38.2bit \
    --meta_file /data/weirauchlab/team/ngun7t/maxatac/training_data/meta_file.tsv \
    --output /data/weirauchlab/team/ngun7t/maxatac/runs/scratch \
    --prefix scratch \
    --epochs 1
fi
"
}

issues: This is a self-submitting pattern: it will only work if `flux batch` can connect to a Flux broker from where the script is executed (inside a Flux instance or via a site-provided submission endpoint).
Portability: requesting a GPU with `-g 1` requires the Flux instance to be configured with GPU/generic resources; otherwise the job may be rejected or remain unschedulable.
The allocation requests 8 tasks (`-n 8`) but only 1 GPU (`-g 1`); if each task expects GPU access, this can oversubscribe the GPU and reduce performance (resource suitability concern).
